reviewer: Kimi actual visual review of the exact 156x210 source, complete opaque RGB raw, unchanged naiwa reference, complete derived RGBA and full white/cyan/alpha sheet/evidence; RGB art and full rectangular painted backplate were approved before running the recorded bilinear source-alpha command, whose stdout JSON receipt was retained and whose RGB/alpha assertions were independently checked again visually.

entries.positive_observation: The dark green-black officer cap retains its glossy visor, gold piping/cords, separate upper eagle and lower wreath/cockade. Short grey temple hair, narrow sideburn edges, pale brows and round thin wire spectacles remain; the cheeks and chin are smooth with no moustache or beard and one serious closed mouth. The slight-left pose, crop and visor shadow remain. The dark olive uniform retains gold shoulder details, pale-piped standing collar, densely gold-embroidered red patches and one black-and-silver throat cross. The rounded chin meets a short broad fitted collar without a stalk or pinching. The continuous pale warm grey-beige painted backplate fills the original rectangle through every corner, with no invented frame, note or replacement backdrop. After the recorded bilinear alpha operation, full derived and sheet viewing confirms the same RGB art/backplate with no visible matte, halo, holes or backing loss.
entries.alpha_decision: The RGB parent was art-approved first. The retained command receipt proves RGB unchanged and resized-source-alpha equality; source/resized/output corners are all [253,253,255,255]. Visual white/cyan inspection, not these numbers alone, found no visible matte or backplate mismatch. No native_alpha_accepted field is asserted for this derived output.
entries.visible_limitations: Fine spectacle rims, cap embroidery, collar oak-leaf detail and the small neck-cross interior are not reliably separable at 156x210; no exact microscopic emblem or glyph is claimed, and these unresolved details are not rejection grounds.
